panels.title: Active sessions (proxy, NOT AWS DB Load/AAS)
panels.description: OPTIONAL/approximation: count of pg_stat_activity rows with state='active'. This is a locally-computed proxy, not the CloudWatch Database Insights DB Load (Average Active Sessions) metric -- see the text panel above and docs/architecture.md.

defaults.description: OPTIONAL/approximation: count of pg_stat_activity rows with state='active'. This is a locally-computed proxy, not the CloudWatch Database Insights DB Load (Average Active Sessions) metric -- see the text panel above and docs/architecture.md.

options.content: **This is NOT the same as CloudWatch Database Insights 'DB Load' (Average Active Sessions).** AWS's Performance Insights feature reached end-of-life on July 31, 2026; existing users were migrated to CloudWatch Database Insights (Standard and Advanced modes). DB Load / AAS is only available via the Performance Insights compatibility API (`GetResourceMetrics` and related `pi:*` actions), which YACE does not and cannot scrape -- YACE only reads ordinary `AWS/RDS` CloudWatch namespace metrics. The panel below is a same-shape *proxy* built from `pg_stat_activity` (count of backends in the `active` state), useful for trend/shape comparison only. See `docs/architecture.md` for the full API boundary, current Database Insights terminology, and an optional, unimplemented collector design.

panels.title: Row modification throughput ($rate_interval)
panels.description: Rate of inserted+updated+deleted rows across user tables. Source: postgres_exporter stat_user_tables collector (enabled by default): pg_stat_user_tables_n_tup_{ins,upd,del}.

defaults.description: Rate of inserted+updated+deleted rows across user tables. Source: postgres_exporter stat_user_tables collector (enabled by default): pg_stat_user_tables_n_tup_{ins,upd,del}.

targets.expr: sum by (cluster, instance) (rate(pg_stat_user_tables_n_tup_ins{cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"}[$rate_interval]) + rate(pg_stat_user_tables_n_tup_upd{cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"}[$rate_interval]) + rate(pg_stat_user_tables_n_tup_del{cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance"}[$rate_interval]))

panels.title: Long-running transactions (OPTIONAL, fleet-wide count/age)
panels.description: OPTIONAL: requires --collector.long_running_transactions (disabled by default upstream and in this repo -- not enabled in systemd/postgres_exporter.service). Source: pg_long_running_transactions (count) and pg_long_running_transactions_oldest_timestamp_seconds (age of the oldest one). Overlaps with the always-on 'Longest running transaction' panel to the left, which is per label set rather than a single fleet-wide count/max-age pair; prefer that built-in unless you specifically need this shape.

defaults.description: OPTIONAL: requires --collector.long_running_transactions (disabled by default upstream and in this repo -- not enabled in systemd/postgres_exporter.service). Source: pg_long_running_transactions (count) and pg_long_running_transactions_oldest_timestamp_seconds (age of the oldest one). Overlaps with the always-on 'Longest running transaction' panel to the left, which is per label set rather than a single fleet-wide count/max-age pair; prefer that built-in unless you specifically need this shape.

panels.description: Commit plus rollback rate over the selected $rate_interval. Source: postgres_exporter stat_database collector (enabled by default).

defaults.description: Commit plus rollback rate over the selected $rate_interval. Source: postgres_exporter stat_database collector (enabled by default).

targets.expr: sum by (cluster, instance) (rate(pg_stat_database_xact_commit{cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$database"}[$rate_interval]) + rate(pg_stat_database_xact_rollback{cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$database"}[$rate_interval]))

panels.description: aurora:rollback_ratio:ratio5m recording rule. A sustained high rollback ratio often indicates application-level retries or constraint violations.

panels.description: OPTIONAL: pg_stat_statements_calls_total (requires --collector.stat_statements).

defaults.description: OPTIONAL: pg_stat_statements_calls_total (requires --collector.stat_statements).

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (queryid, datname) (rate(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{cluster=~"$cluster", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$database"}[$rate_interval])))

panels.description: OPTIONAL: pg_stat_statements_seconds_total (requires --collector.stat_statements).

defaults.description: OPTIONAL: pg_stat_statements_seconds_total (requires --collector.stat_statements).

options.content: **OPTIONAL.** Every panel in this row requires the `stat_statements` postgres_exporter collector, which is DISABLED by default upstream (and in this repo's systemd unit) because it is high-cardinality on busy servers, and requires the `pg_stat_statements` extension to be created and added to `shared_preload_libraries` first -- see `sql/create_monitoring_role.sql` and `docs/metrics-reference.md`. Enable with `--collector.stat_statements` once you have assessed the cardinality impact.

panels.title: Oldest unfrozen transaction ID age
panels.description: OPTIONAL (requires --collector.database_wraparound, enabled in this repo's systemd unit but disabled upstream by default): pg_database_wraparound_age_datfrozenxid_seconds. NOTE: despite the '_seconds' suffix inherited from the exporter's metric-name convention, the value is a transaction-ID AGE (a count), not a time duration -- see docs/metrics-reference.md. PostgreSQL forces read-only mode at age 2,146,483,648.

defaults.description: OPTIONAL (requires --collector.database_wraparound, enabled in this repo's systemd unit but disabled upstream by default): pg_database_wraparound_age_datfrozenxid_seconds. title: Aurora PostgreSQL Observability
description: Provisionable overview dashboard for Aurora PostgreSQL: postgres_exporter engine metrics plus optional AWS/RDS CloudWatch metrics via YACE. Panels marked OPTIONAL depend on a non-default collector flag, the pg_stat_statements extension, or the yace scrape job being configured. See docs/dashboard-guide.md.
